one_line: Shared map-and-timeline trip planner co-edited by a human and browser agent.
what_it_does: Plans a multi-day trip into a live map and timed itinerary, with reviewable agent edits, deterministic routing and shared revision state.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central because the agent and person mutate and inspect the same structured spatial itinerary, including pending edits, revision history, and human changes; UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes human and agent co-editing one live map and schedule.
About text describes shared store, pending/revert/accept workflow, get_itinerary and get_changes state reads.
execution_rationale: The video sheets show a coherent map-centered product with itinerary cards and populated route/result states. The described review and scheduling workflow is ambitious and appears substantially demonstrated, though exact end-to-end tool details are not legible.
execution_evidence: Video sheets visibly show map routes/markers alongside itinerary and place panels.
Video evidence progresses from planning UI to a populated spatial itinerary.
impact_rationale: Travelers have a clear problem: turning agent-generated plans into an editable, spatial, reviewable itinerary without copy-paste. The shared map and schedule directly address that workflow.
impact_evidence: Description identifies the copy-paste gap between AI itineraries and maps apps.
Video shows a usable itinerary/map result.
creativity_rationale: Shared human-agent ownership of a live spatial schedule, with pending edits and deterministic schedule computation, is a notably fresh interaction model for trip planning.
creativity_evidence: Agent edits are reviewable in place rather than delivered as chat text.
Concept combines map, timeline, revision fates, and shared agent state.
usability_note: Clear map-plus-itinerary workflow; review states may add complexity but preserve control.
advance_reason: High leverage and impact with credible product-motion evidence and a distinctive shared spatial workflow.

one_line: Human-reviewed food-rescue matching planner for surplus meals and community kitchens.
what_it_does: Matches donor meal offers to kitchens under capacity, dietary, allergen, travel, and time constraints, while coordinators protect commitments and review staged replans.
leverage_rationale: The structured agent surface makes constraint-heavy planning, explanations, what-if analysis, and staged proposals substantially more reliable than generic UI automation, while keeping the coordinator in control.
leverage_evidence: About describes read-only what-if planning, rejection explanations, capacity updates, and staged proposals.
Protected commitments are preserved through the same live planning workspace.
execution_rationale: The video shows a coherent operational dashboard with meal records, assignments, and review states. The deterministic flow solver and explicit shortfall scenario indicate strong scope completion, although no real dispatch is claimed.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show populated food/assignment records and coordinator review panels.
Description provides a concrete 480-to-410 portions replanning scenario with protected commitments.
impact_rationale: Food-rescue coordinators face real, high-consequence allocation constraints; preserving commitments and surfacing shortages instead of hiding them is directly valuable.
impact_evidence: Specific donor-to-kitchen matching use case with allergen and capacity constraints.
Demonstrated scenario reports protected 120 portions and an explicit 70-portion shortfall.
creativity_rationale: Applying shared agent state, explainable rejection reasons, protected commitments, and human approval to food rescue is an original and thoughtfully constrained use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Human-agent planning is framed around commitments and last-minute operational changes.
Deterministic min-cost flow is paired with reviewable agent proposals.
usability_note: Operational cards and review controls look legible; constraint-heavy planning could still demand training.
red_flags: Synthetic data and planning-only scope; no actual deliveries.
standouts: Explicit, honest shortfall handling and protected commitments.
advance_reason: Exceptional real-world value and strong agent-in-workspace design, with credible visual evidence.

one_line: Agent-ready circuit canvas that builds, simulates, and exports firmware from one live graph.
what_it_does: Lets an agent place components, connect pins, simulate digital logic, and generate Arduino/ESP32-oriented firmware while a user sees the same circuit state.
leverage_rationale: Structured graph operations and simulation are central: an agent can reliably construct and test circuits without coordinate-driven canvas manipulation, then use the same state for firmware export.
leverage_evidence: Four tools cover placement, pin connection, simulation, and firmware export.
About describes a live graph shared by agent and user and a half-adder built and tested through the workflow.
execution_rationale: The video visibly presents a coherent dark circuit-design environment with diagrams, console/output panels, and generated technical output. The claimed half-adder workflow covers construction, all input combinations, verification, and export.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show circuit editor/graph, console-like activity, and output/code surfaces.
Description specifies four simulation cases with expected Sum and Carry verification before firmware export.
impact_rationale: Students, makers, and embedded developers can reduce friction between circuit prototyping, validation, and firmware preparation; the integrated workflow addresses a genuine toolchain gap.
impact_evidence: Clear audience of circuit designers and IoT/Arduino prototypers.
Video shows design and simulation/output surfaces in one environment.
creativity_rationale: A shared agent-operated circuit graph that goes from natural-language hardware intent through simulation to firmware is ambitious and memorable, beyond a generic code copilot.
creativity_evidence: Combines visual circuit construction, live signals, logic simulation, and firmware generation.
Agent Activity Console exposes calls, latency, payloads, and results.
usability_note: Dense engineering UI is appropriate to the audience; graph and console complexity may challenge novices.
standouts: Strong end-to-end technical workflow and highly consequential structured state.
advance_reason: Near-transformative WebMCP leverage, demonstrated technical workflow, and high ambition.

one_line: Agent-native marketplace for discovering, verifying, and comparing African travel packages.
what_it_does: Searches representative packages, verifies agencies, compares options, and prepares contact while reserving booking and payment for human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, verification, comparison, and shortlist state improve research reliability and preserve approval boundaries, but a capable agent could achieve much of the discovery workflow through ordinary browsing with friction.
leverage_evidence: About lists five WebMCP tools for package search and comparison workflow.
Agent updates filters, selected comparisons, shortlist count, and verification evidence in the same interface.
execution_rationale: Video sheets show a coherent travel marketplace progressing from criteria/search to populated package cards and comparison-oriented states. The visual evidence supports a functional scoped demo.
execution_evidence: Video shows search forms, travel result cards, details, and selection controls.
Final states visibly contain populated travel options rather than only a landing page.
impact_rationale: Travelers dealing with fragmented African package information and uncertain agencies have a specific research and trust problem that comparison and verification can materially improve.
impact_evidence: Description identifies fragmented WhatsApp, social, and agency-web offers.
Video shows marketplace results and comparison/selection surfaces.
creativity_rationale: The candidate-controlled, agent-native travel marketplace focuses on verification and consequential-decision boundaries rather than another itinerary chatbot, a fresh synthesis for the domain.
creativity_evidence: Agent researches and prepares contact but does not book or pay.
Verification evidence is returned alongside package comparison.
usability_note: Familiar marketplace presentation with a clear human approval boundary.
red_flags: Representative packages and agency verification appear demo-scoped.
standouts: Strong trust/control framing for consequential travel decisions.
advance_reason: Clear audience need, polished scoped marketplace workflow, and meaningful structured-agent benefit.

one_line: Shared calendar planner that finds availability and stages preference-aware conflict resolutions.
what_it_does: Inspects scoped calendar context, ranks meeting options, and prepares bounded reschedules or time-away change sets for explicit human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Calendar semantics, privacy boundaries, revisioned drafts, idempotency, and explicit confirmation make structured tools materially safer and more precise than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: About specifies narrow context reads, weekly availability checks, privacy-preserving Busy blocks, and reviewed draft revisions.
Agent cannot apply changes or notify users; human confirmation is required.
execution_rationale: The video shows a dense but coherent calendar product with populated events, planning dialogs, and schedule states. The bounded workflow is well specified, though full application of changes is intentionally outside the agent path.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show calendar grids, event blocks, and modal/side-panel scheduling states.
Description details conflict checking and before/after diff confirmation.
impact_rationale: Distributed teams and people coordinating around focus time, travel, time zones, and privacy have a real scheduling burden; preference-aware proposals with human ownership directly address it.
impact_evidence: Specific distributed launch-team use case and recurring scheduling constraints.
Video visibly shows populated calendar and conflict/planning states.
creativity_rationale: The combination of privacy-preserving context, bounded change sets, human-reviewed diffs, and one-time idempotent confirmation is a thoughtful interaction model for agent scheduling.
creativity_evidence: Private events remain generic Busy outside owner access.
Agent prepares compact, reviewable change sets rather than broad write access.
usability_note: Familiar calendar layout and explicit diffs support trust, though the safety protocol adds steps.
red_flags: Seeded demo calendar rather than connected production calendars.
standouts: Excellent safety and privacy boundaries around agent scheduling.
advance_reason: High-impact productivity problem with unusually strong structured-state and human-control design.

one_line: Voice-driven job-search and application assistant that operates forms through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Uses a voice agent to search/filter jobs and fill repetitive application fields hands-free, asking for personal input and refusing final submission.
leverage_rationale: Directly exposed page controls reduce both vision-agent misclicks and screen-reader traversal for multi-step forms; WebMCP changes reliability and accessibility of form interaction.
leverage_evidence: About contrasts coordinate-guessing vision bots and slow screen-reader tab traversal.
Product exposes buttons and inputs directly to a voice agent and preserves human submission.
execution_rationale: The video visibly demonstrates a voice/video interaction paired with dark application panels and updated application content. The core interaction appears real, but fine-grained form completion and tool details are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show human voice/video presence, agent/status or transcript panels, and changing application UI.
Packaging and description consistently present a voice-driven form workflow.
impact_rationale: Job applicants with visual impairment, hand/wrist limitations, or hands-busy contexts have a concrete accessibility and repetitive-form burden; hands-free page-native interaction addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Description identifies screen-reader and vision-bot barriers and concrete affected users.
Video shows voice interaction leading to updated web application content.
creativity_rationale: Combining voice conversation, page-native semantic controls, accessibility, and deliberate refusal to submit creates a compelling human-agent application model.
creativity_evidence: Voice agent asks for user input on personal fields and refuses legal submission.
Uses WebMCP alongside Gemini Live/OpenAI Realtime for direct page interaction.
usability_note: Hands-free interaction is promising; voice latency and form edge cases remain likely concerns.
red_flags: The visible demo uses a careers-site/demo context; production-site integration is not established.
standouts: Accessibility is a substantive product driver, not a cosmetic voice layer.
advance_reason: High impact and strong WebMCP rationale, with visible voice-to-UI product evidence.

one_line: WebMCP-native trail planner for verified hiking loops around Barcelona.
what_it_does: Selects and validates graph-verified routes against distance and context, then renders a shared map, route evidence, forecast, daylight, and park notices.
leverage_rationale: The agent works over verified route graphs and shared spatial state, validating a closed circuit before rendering it; this is materially safer and more precise than generic map UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About emphasizes shared map, route evidence, limitations, and graph-verified circuit options.
Agent validates routes before changing the map and records actions in a shared worklog/trail ledger.
execution_rationale: Video sheets show a coherent green hiking-planning interface with populated plan cards and supporting information. The stated route validation and briefing/GPX scope appears substantial, though map detail is not always legible in the sheets.
execution_evidence: Video shows populated hiking plan/document panels and supporting trip information.
Description specifies route rendering, measured distance/ascent, forecasts, daylight, and notices.
impact_rationale: Hikers and trail runners need trustworthy route selection and current constraints; verified loops and clearly labeled planning context address safety and planning friction.
impact_evidence: Specific audience and local trail-planning problem are clearly described.
Product visibly presents structured trip-planning results.
creativity_rationale: Treating a hike as a shared spatial decision with graph verification, evidence, and a trail ledger is a strong, domain-specific interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent and person inspect the same route and limitations.
Human retains manual control over briefing review and GPX download.
usability_note: Structured cards and map context support review; information density may be high for casual hikers.
red_flags: Geographic scope is intentionally limited to Collserola/Vallvidrera.
standouts: Ground-truth route verification and shared spatial review.
advance_reason: Strong niche impact and differentiated verified-route collaboration with credible visual product evidence.

one_line: Analyst-first security workbench where bounded agents investigate while humans retain authority.
what_it_does: Runs approved investigation skills, exposes exact KQL and raw records, builds a live evidence graph, and prepares—but does not autonomously approve—responses.
leverage_rationale: Bounded, revision-scoped investigation tools give agents structured access to evidence and fixed KQL contracts while preserving analyst gates; generic UI driving would be less auditable and safe.
leverage_evidence: About specifies exact KQL, raw records, live evidence graph, and fixed contracts preventing query widening.
Evidence sufficiency, response approval, and closure remain analyst-controlled.
execution_rationale: The video clearly shows a coherent dark security operations workbench with logs, evidence panels, statuses, and investigation controls. Synthetic data and response recording are appropriate to the stated demo scope.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show dense analyst tables/log panels and evidence-oriented investigation views.
Description states the central investigation workflow and synthetic-data boundary.
impact_rationale: Security analysts need faster investigation without losing evidence traceability or authority; the product directly addresses that high-value operational tension.
impact_evidence: Specific SOC analyst audience and case-investigation workflow.
Video visibly presents evidence/log organization and human review controls.
creativity_rationale: The analyst-first design makes bounded agent investigation, evidence sufficiency, and approval gates first-class rather than bolting a summary onto a SIEM.
creativity_evidence: Live evidence graph and exact raw records accompany agent work.
Agent prepares response but cannot take consequential action.
usability_note: The dense analyst surface is appropriate but likely has a steep learning curve.
red_flags: Synthetic telemetry; real SIEM/EDR integrations are future work.
standouts: Excellent evidence custody and analyst authority boundaries.
advance_reason: High-impact operational workflow with strong evidence-backed execution and careful agent boundaries.

one_line: Candidate-side investigation workspace for interviewing and due-diligencing a job role.
what_it_does: Separates employer claims from unresolved candidate questions, corroborates official sources, and recomputes investigation priorities as shared case state changes.
leverage_rationale: Shared case state and structured evidence make iterative due diligence more coherent than chat, but much of the research could still be performed by a general agent with real friction.
leverage_evidence: About describes shared case updates, priority changes, recomputed investigation targets, and source corroboration.
Product distinguishes stated facts from unresolved lived-work questions.
execution_rationale: The video shows a coherent question-and-answer/role-evaluation interface with populated cards and role information. The core investigation workflow is visible, though source research depth is difficult to verify from frames alone.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show sequential questions, responses, role data, and summary/evaluation panels.
Description provides a concrete travel-requirement corroboration example.
impact_rationale: Job candidates make costly career decisions with incomplete job-description information; separating published claims from unresolved questions provides credible decision support.
impact_evidence: Clear candidate-side due-diligence audience and problem.
Video shows consolidated role/interview information rather than a simple fit score.
creativity_rationale: Interviewing the job and modeling the gap between literal JD claims and lived work is a memorable, original framing with a useful investigation interaction.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly rejects another generic fit score.
Priority changes can alter the next investigation target through shared state.
usability_note: Question-and-card workflow is approachable; research terminology may require explanation.
red_flags: Some real-world research claims are not independently visible in the demo frames.
standouts: Strong candidate-centered reframing of job search due diligence.
advance_reason: Distinctive, credible candidate value with a coherent investigation workspace and visible product flow.

one_line: Napoleonic real-time strategy game with an agent operating through the same live match state.
what_it_does: Lets players command units and formations while an agent reads the battlefield, issues orders, and writes standing rules that execute in the simulation.
leverage_rationale: The agent's structured access to the live, fast-changing simulation and standing-order interface enables parallel strategic control that screen-driving cannot replicate comparably well; WebMCP is core to the intended experience.
leverage_evidence: Nineteen tools expose the whole live match without screenshots or pointer control.
Standing orders let the game execute agent-authored rules between slow model reactions while sharing one match object.
execution_rationale: The video sheets visibly show an evolving dark RTS with battlefield, units, colored regions, command overlays, and status panels. The described scope is coherent and technically ambitious, though the exact complete match outcome is not fully established by small frames.
execution_evidence: Video shows game-like battlefield states, units, tactical overlays, and information panels.
Description explains a single command layer shared by UI and tools and a 20-tick simulation.
impact_rationale: For strategy-game players, preserving simulation depth while delegating concurrent monitoring and orders creates genuine entertainment and accessibility value; the audience and desire are clear.
impact_evidence: Specific RTS player problem: simulation depth exceeds one player's attention capacity.
Video visibly demonstrates a populated tactical game state.
creativity_rationale: An RTS designed around an agent as a parallel commander, plus standing orders that bridge model latency, is an unusually inventive interaction model deeply tied to the medium.
creativity_evidence: Agent acts alongside the player through its own interface rather than taking over the screen.
Standing orders solve the real-time mismatch between agent calls and a 20-tick game.
usability_note: The game intentionally carries high information density; the agent helps, but the overall system may be demanding to learn.
red_flags: No public repository is listed; eligibility depends on challenge rules not visible in the packet.
standouts: Most transformative agent/game interaction and a compelling standing-order solution.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and creativity, with visible game product evidence; eligibility is the only material uncertainty.
